title: Event Evidence (fact_event_evidence)
description: One evidence item supporting, contradicting or contextualising a fact_event. Distinct from schemas/evidence.schema.json, which remains the frozen WO-002-era contract for reviewed_event records: this contract adds the source-class discovery/confirmation distinction and the excerpt-length bound required by WO-010 Gate D and G, and is used by the Ocean event model.

claim.description: A bounded statement of what this source says. Bounded deliberately: the platform records the claim and links to the source, and never republishes a full copyrighted article.

evidence_role.description: Whether this item may carry a material conclusion. A discovery source may detect a lead but may never be the sole evidence for a material impact conclusion; 'discovery_only' marks items that are structurally barred from doing so.

strength.description: Evidence strength. Read together with strength_basis: an 'expected_at_cutoff' grading is what the case asserts, not a verified assessment of retrieved content.

retrieved_at.description: When the source content was actually retrieved. Null unless retrieval_status is 'retrieved'; a historical fixture whose content was never fetched has no retrieval time.

content_sha256.description: Content hash, scoped by content_hash_scope. For a fixture this is a claim-record hash over this repository's own authored text, and is not evidence about any publisher response.

raw_snapshot_path.description: Always null in the public repository. Raw responses, caches and restricted content must not enter the public repository.

intended_source_id.description: For a fixture, the publisher this evidence stands in for. Never a claim that the content came from there.

strength_basis.description: Whether 'strength' is a verified grading of retrieved content, or the strength the authored case asserts would have been available at its cutoff. A fixture can only ever be 'expected_at_cutoff'.

dataset.description: The publication surface this evidence belongs to. Carried at record level: an evidence item cited by a current assessment must itself be current.
